title: Adic completion is Noetherian when the quotient is Noetherian and the ideal finitely generated
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal such that (1) the quotient ring $R/I$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and (2) $I$ is finitely generated. Let $R^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR/I^n$ be the $I$-adic completion of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and $IR^\wedge$ the ideal of $R^\wedge$ generated by the image of $I$ under the canonical map $R\to R^\wedge$. Then $R^\wedge$ is a Noetherian ring and $R^\wedge$ is $IR^\wedge$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring].

proof.text: Put A=AdicCompletion I R and J=I.map(algebraMap R A). The ideal J is finitely generated by Ideal.FG.map. Mathlib 05GG supplies I-adic completeness of A; IsAdicComplete.map_algebraMap_iff converts this to J-adic completeness.
The surjective evalOne algebra map A→R/I has kernel J by 05GG. The first isomorphism theorem gives A/J≃R/I, and its inverse transports Noetherianity to A/J.
Apply the finite-type associated graded theorem to the finitely generated ideal J. Since A/J is Noetherian, Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing makes gr_J(A) Noetherian.

For each ideal K of A use J-adic completeness and Noetherianity of gr_J(A) to obtain K.FG. The equivalence isNoetherianRing_iff_ideal_fg gives Noetherianity of A. Pair this with the completeness already proved.

split_report.summary: Split along the proof of Stacks 05GH (algebra.tex lines 23022-23063), tags 05GH, 05GG, 00FN verified in tags/tags. Step 1: completeness of R^ w.r.t. IR^ and R^/IR^ = R/I from the existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal (05GG), Noetherianity of R^/IR^ via lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian, reduction to a J-adically complete A with J=(g_1..g_t), A/J Noetherian. Step 2: gr_J(A) is a quotient of (A/J)[T_1..T_t] (def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring), hence Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian. Steps 3-6: the initial ideal G(K) of an ideal K has homogeneous generators lifting to h_j in K, the approximation x - sum a_j h_j in K cap J^{n+1}, the iteration, and the convergence of A_j = sum_n a_{j,n} by completeness, with x - sum A_j h_j in the intersection of the J^k, which is 0; written out where Stacks says 'as R is complete'. New node: def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring (unsplit, not in Mathlib). Not a Mathlib leaf (LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, grep). Statement unchanged; stmt_deps unchanged.
